label: copy phase: echoed input is one of p/d/o/f/r/i/b/m/a, with build-up over the sequence
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires in the original phase, at <DEL>, or at the first copy output. The main driver is the token fed back as input: p has the highest rate (29%), then d, o, f (18-20%), r, i, then b, m, a (about 10%). h and 0 are below the base rate. Activation seems to build up and decay over consecutive steps: it peaks on a set token that comes after earlier set tokens (for example ...f p j 3 gives 0.82, 0.81, 0.55, 0.31) and sometimes carries over weakly to the next one or two non-set inputs, which accounts for most of the missed activations (about 8% of mass). Rate rises with recall_idx and L (29% at the last step of L=9). Requiring at least 3 set tokens among the earlier inputs gives dev F1 0.54 and mass recall 0.80. Precision stays low (about 0.43): many set-token copy steps do not fire, so the predicate is incomplete.
